scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 14 · KP08 Hierarchical clustering for large data

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: CURE: pick a few well-scattered representatives per cluster, then shrink them toward the mean

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: blue is the elongated group $A$ (outlier at top right), orange the round group $B$; hollow rings are representatives, filled dots after shrinking, stars the means, the green line the closest representative pair, red rings misassigned points.

scene-u01-pnew1-226.name: text#226
scene-u01-pnew1-226.text: Pick the point farthest from the mean

scene-u01-pnew1-230.name: text#230
scene-u01-pnew1-230.text: Repeatedly pick the point farthest from those chosen, $k$ in total

scene-u01-pnew1-234.name: text#234
scene-u01-pnew1-234.text: Shrink each representative toward the mean

scene-u01-pnew1-238.name: text#238
scene-u01-pnew1-238.text: Cluster distance: the minimum over representative pairs

scene-u01-pnew1-243.name: text#243
scene-u01-pnew1-243.text: With a sample of $N'$ points, worst-case cost drops from $O(N^2\log_2N)$ to $O(N'^2\log_2N')$; at $N'=2.5\%N$ that is about $2354$ times less [Added].

scene-u01-pnew1-245.name: text#245
scene-u01-pnew1-245.text: Demo data and numbers computed by code

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 14 · KP08 Hierarchical clustering for large data

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: ROCK: for categorical data, count common neighbors instead of distances

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: each circle is a basket (item numbers below), linked only if Jaccard is at least $0.5$; the table gives the common-neighbor count $\mathrm{link}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$.

scene-u01-pnew2-234.name: text#234
scene-u01-pnew2-234.text: All zero across the sets: they never merge

scene-u01-pnew2-236.name: text#236
scene-u01-pnew2-236.text: Merge score: observed cross links over expected cross links

scene-u01-pnew2-242.name: text#242
scene-u01-pnew2-242.text: Once each set merges into one cluster, all cross links are $0$ and the algorithm stops; basket $9$ stays alone as an outlier. $f(\theta)$ is a strong assumption.

scene-u01-pnew2-244.name: text#244
scene-u01-pnew2-244.text: Demo data and numbers computed by code

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 14 · KP08 Hierarchical clustering for large data

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Chameleon: merge only if the link between clusters is strong relative to their insides

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left shows the four clusters of Example 13.10 (numbers are edge similarities, $|E_i|$ the internal min-cut bisection); the right compares cross similarity, $RI$, $RC$ and $RI\cdot RC^2$ for two pairs.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Example 13.10: $C_3,C_4$ are closer ($0.6>0.4$) but much tighter inside

scene-u01-pnew3-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew3-53.text: MST sees only the first bars (orange higher); Chameleon uses the other three (blue higher)

scene-u01-pnew3-60.name: text#60
scene-u01-pnew3-60.text: Tighter clusters have larger denominators and resist merging; Chameleon first divides ($k$-nearest-neighbor graph, min cut) and then agglomerates.
